text.p: Here are highlights of stories reported by Hungary's press, based on information by Nepszabadsag's Hungary Around the Clock service. For further details on how to subscribe to Hungary Around the Clock, please contact Monica Kovacs at (361) 351 7142 or fax your request to (361) 351 7141.
ALL PAPERS
- NATO Secretary General Javier Solana said during a stopover at Ferihegy airport on Wednesday that Turkey will not veto the eastward expansion of the military alliance.
- The government will cut several ministries' annual budgets to a total value of HUF 8 billion in order to meet the central budget's salary targets.
- Prime Minister Gyula Horn has put off plans to visit Canada next week, on the advice of his doctors.

- Foreign Minister Laszlo Kovacs said that Hungary has repeatedly proposed, since the Slovak language law was passed last year, that a law on the use of minority languages consistent with the needs of the Hungarian minority also be enacted in Slovakia.

- Sandor Lezsak, president of the Democratic Forum said his party has a vested interest in having a strong Christian Democratic Party as its ally, but it will continue to beef up ties with the reliable Young Democrats.

- The State Privatisation and Holding Co. decided that one or both of two state-owned banks will screen the Polgari Bank in two weeks, then stabilise it by a capital injection to help prepare Polgari for its privatisation.
- A total of 84,000 people have been downed by a nationwide flu epidemic, now in its third week.
- Skala-Coop will raise its stake in fellow retailer Centrum from its current 25 percent to 41 percent.
MAGYAR HIRLAP
- Young Democrat president Viktor Orban said in an interview that his party is obliged to treat as a fact the evolution of two power groups on the opposition side.

- The board of management of the State Privatisation and Holding Co. on Wednesday imposed (undetermined) sanctions on former director general Istvan Kocsis and Miklos Kamaras for their "indirect responsibility" in the Tocsik affair. The board also decided to reclaim the HUF 804 million fee paid to lawyer Marta Tocsik.
- The State Privatisation and Holding Co. revealed that it received total revenues of HUF 157.9 billion last year and spent HUF 148 billion.
VILAGGAZDASAG
- The financial status of the Hungarian airline Malev and a concept for its further privatisation will be on the cabinet's agenda at its meeting today.

- Talks towards resolving a World Trade Organisation dispute have made no progress as the WTO has rejected a Hungarian proposal that 1995 subsidy levels rather than those specified in a GATT agreement signed in 1992 be used as a base for phasing out agricultural export subsidies.

- The German company Linde-KCA-Dresden GmbH, a subsidiary of Line AG in Wiesbaden, has been chosen to construct a DM100 million state-of-the-art pharmaceutical production facility for Richter Gedeon in Budapest.
- This paper reports that EBRD and the IFC are prepared to purchase a 30 percent stake in the state-owned agricultural company Babolna Rt.
NEPSZABADSAG
- Unemployment stood at 10.6 percent at the end of January as 474,600 people were registered jobless.
NAPI GAZDASAG
- Economic growth in Hungary may reach 3 percent this year, according to a study by HBSC James Capel.
- OTP Bank will bid for the state-owned Penzintezeti Kozpont Bank.
-- Budapest newsroom (36 1) 327 4040
